- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to reflect risk reversal.  
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) — cap forecast increase to 3% max after spike.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 68–70), model often holds too high — reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 2–3 periods.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum — if sentiment turns positive mid-horizon, adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% per day for final 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +0.67, -0.33, +0.67), model tends to lag — add 0.5–1% buffer to forecast for next 3–5 days.
